title: Tenant-aware latency-gradient lane allocator for prefill/decode scheduling
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Our current prefill/decode arbitration tilts toward aggregate throughput under heavy load, causing tail latency regressions for small, latency-sensitive tenants and bursty interactive workloads. In addition, kernel selection heuristics are not tightly coupled with per-request phase expectations (prefill vs decode) so some requests are routed to slower kernels during critical decode phases.

Proposal: Implement a tenant-aware latency-gradient lane allocator (LGLA) that dynamically creates lightweight lanes with explicit latency gradients and maps requests to lanes based on a compact latency priority score. LGLA will: 1) split requests into phase-aware micro-lanes (prefill-optimized vs decode-optimized) using request metadata and expected sequence length; 2) apply tenant-aware fairness budgets so tenant weight and latency-sensitivity influence lane assignment; 3) feed lane-level signals to kernel selection so the runtime prefers low-latency kernel variants during decode lanes while allowing throughput-optimized kernels in background lanes; 4) support opportunistic hedging and admission control when headroom is limited.

Why different: This approach encodes latency SLOs as a continuous gradient across soft lanes rather than strict priority buckets, enabling proportional fairness while preserving throughput when capacity allows. It explicitly couples scheduling lanes with kernel-selection hints to reduce tail latency during decode-critical windows.
acceptance_criteria: Latency-sensitive tenant P99 tail improves by >=20% on p50 load tests compared to baseline for 2k token avg workloads
Overall throughput (tokens/sec) remains within -5% of baseline under mixed workload at 70% GPU utilization
Kernel-selection telemetry shows increased selection of low-latency kernels for decode lanes with noise <5% across runs
Feature flags exist to enable LGLA, hedging, and lane-to-kernel hints separately
Unit + integration tests for lane assignment logic and kernel hint propagation in CI
Canary rollout plan documented and automated to revert in <5 minutes
tasks: Draft design RFC and metric definitions (latency gradient score formula)
Prototype lane allocator in runtime simulator and run microbenchmarks
Add kernel-hint API to scheduler -> kernel-selector interface
Implement tenant-weighted fairness accounting and soft budgets
Integrate hedging/admission fallbacks and safe defaults
End-to-end tests with mixed prefills/decodes and per-tenant SLAs
Dashboard panels for lane utilization, kernel-choice breakdown, and per-tenant tail latency
Canary rollout (10% traffic) and A/B evaluation on production-like workload
comments: 2026-02-11 - Ava Martinez: Initial problem statement posted. Collected latency regression examples from support tickets 9981 and 10002. Shared trace snippets in #runtime-performance.

2026-02-13 - Rohit Patel: Ran simulator for simple two-lane split. Observed 18% P99 improvement for decode-heavy tenants but throughput dropped 7% at 85% utilization. Need kernel hint coupling to recover throughput.
2026-02-15 - Emily Chen (review): Design looks promising. Question: how do we prevent lane starvation for low-priority tenants during sustained spikes? Suggest tenant soft-credits that decay slowly.
2026-02-17 - Rohit Patel: Added tenant soft-credits and proportional refill algorithm in prototype. Updated acceptance criteria to allow -5% throughput delta.
2026-02-18 - Security (note): No secrets or new data flows. Kernel-hint API reviewed; no changes required to KMS/Audit.
2026-02-19 - Rohit Patel: Opened draft PR for simulator code and kernel-hint interface: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8421
2026-02-20 - PM triage (Ana Lopes): Prioritized for cycle 2026-W07. Ensure telemetry events include tenant_id hashed and lane_id for downstream privacy-preserving analytics.
notes: Trade-offs: tight latency gradients reduce throughput headroom during sustained load; we mitigate this with soft budgets and kernel demotion policies. Rollout must include aggressive observability and an automated revert path.
implementation_approach: Phase 1: Simulation + kernel-hint API (no prod changes). Phase 2: Runtime canary with LGLA disabled by default (control plane flags). Phase 3: Enable by tenant segment and measure SLA improvements. Each phase gated by acceptance criteria.
